long_biography.plain_text:
While studying medicine at Universidade Nova de Lisboa, Mirpuri proposed turning his family's flight department into a commercial venture. He founded Air Luxor, then helped establish NetJets Europe and served as its first president. After selling Air Luxor, he founded Hi Fly in 2005 and developed it into a global provider of aircraft, crew, maintenance and insurance capacity.

Mirpuri remained Hi Fly's chairman until his death in 2026. He also developed aviation-support businesses in maintenance, inflight catering, airport management and ground handling. A qualified physician and Airbus pilot, he founded the Mirpuri Foundation to support medical research, environmental conservation, humanitarian work and the arts. Competitive sailing became another defining pursuit, expressed through ocean-racing teams, youth training and conservation campaigns.

According to the classification society RINA, Green Eyes is registered to Hi Fly Ltd, a company owned by Paulo Mirpuri, who serves as the President and CEO. Paulo Mirpuri, based in Lisbon, Portugal, leads Hi Fly, a prominent European company specializing in Wet Leasing. Operating globally, Hi Fly manages a fleet of 11 modern Airbus aircraft. They offer clients complete services, including aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance, making them a preferred choice for airlines and governments. Hi Fly operates through two affiliated airlines located in Portugal and Malta.

In addition to his involvement with Hi Fly, Mr. Mirpuri holds positions in various other companies. He is the President of LSKY, a company that specializes in inflight catering, and MESA, a provider of aircraft line maintenance. Furthermore, he serves as the President of Safeport, a company that provides ground services for Business Jets.

It is worth noting that Paulo Mirpuri participated in the annual 2022 Mirpuri Foundation Sailing Trophy, which was organized by the Mirpuri Foundation.
